SOFTWARE AS A SERVICE AGREEMENT

This Software as a Service Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of
February 1, 2026 (the "Effective Date"), by and between:

Acme Cloud Inc., a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business
at 500 Enterprise Way, Suite 1200, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 ("Provider"); and

TechStart LLC, a California limited liability company, with its principal place
of business at 88 Startup Boulevard, Suite 400, Palo Alto, California 94301
("Customer").

Provider and Customer are each referred to herein as a "Party" and collectively
as the "Parties."

WHEREAS, Provider has developed and operates a cloud-based software platform
that provides data analytics, workflow automation, and business intelligence
services (the "Platform"); and

WHEREAS, Customer desires to subscribe to and use the Platform, and Provider
desires to provide Customer with access to the Platform, subject to the terms
and conditions set forth herein;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, agreements, and
representations contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration,
the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree
as follows:


1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is
controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, where "control" means
the ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or
equivalent ownership interest.

1.2 "Authorized Users" means Customer's employees, contractors, and agents who
are authorized by Customer to access and use the Platform under this Agreement,
subject to the user limits specified in the applicable Order Form.

1.3 "Confidential Information" means any non-public information disclosed by
one Party to the other, whether orally, in writing, or by inspection, that is
designated as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be
confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of
disclosure. Confidential Information includes, without limitation, trade
secrets, know-how, inventions, techniques, processes, algorithms, software
programs, source code, object code, customer lists, financial information,
business plans, and marketing strategies.

1.4 "Customer Data" means all electronic data, information, content, and
materials submitted, uploaded, or transmitted by or on behalf of Customer or
its Authorized Users to the Platform in the course of using the Services.

1.5 "Documentation" means Provider's standard user manuals, online help files,
and technical documentation for the Platform, as updated by Provider from time
to time.

1.6 "Feedback" means any suggestions, enhancement requests, recommendations,
corrections, or other feedback provided by Customer or its Authorized Users
regarding the Platform or Services.

1.7 "Intellectual Property Rights" means all patent rights, copyright rights,
moral rights, rights of publicity, trademark and trade dress rights, goodwill,
trade secret rights, and any other intellectual property rights as may exist now
or hereafter come into existence, including all applications and registrations,
renewals, and extensions thereof.

1.8 "Order Form" means the ordering document executed by the Parties that
references this Agreement and specifies the Services, subscription tier, number
of Authorized Users, Fees, and subscription term.

1.9 "Services" means the Platform, Documentation, and any professional
services, support, or maintenance provided by Provider to Customer under this
Agreement and any applicable Order Form.

1.10 "Service Level Agreement" or "SLA" means the service level commitments
set forth in Exhibit A attached hereto, as may be updated by Provider from time
to time upon thirty (30) days' written notice to Customer.

1.11 "Subscription Term" means the period during which Customer has the right
to access and use the Platform, as specified in the applicable Order Form.

1.12 "Third-Party Components" means any third-party software, libraries,
modules, or services that are incorporated into or used in connection with the
Platform.

1.13 "Usage Data" means data generated by the Platform relating to Customer's
use of the Services, including system logs, performance metrics, and aggregated
usage statistics, but excluding Customer Data.

1.14 "Work Product" means any and all inventions, discoveries, improvements,
ideas, concepts, techniques, methods, processes, designs, software, code,
algorithms, documentation, reports, analyses, and other works of authorship or
materials, whether or not patentable or copyrightable, whether or not related
to Provider's business, that are created, conceived, developed, or reduced to
practice by Customer, its employees, or its Authorized Users during the term
of this Agreement, whether independently or jointly with Provider.

1.15 "Virus" means any software routine, device, or mechanism, including any
virus, worm, Trojan horse, or other malicious code, designed to disable,
delete, damage, or interfere with the proper operation of any software, hardware,
or network.


2. GRANT OF LICENSE; RESTRICTIONS

2.1 License Grant. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and
Customer's payment of all applicable Fees, Provider hereby grants to Customer a
non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, limited right to access and
use the Platform during the Subscription Term, solely for Customer's internal
business purposes and in accordance with the Documentation and any usage
limitations specified in the applicable Order Form.

2.2 Authorized Users. Customer may permit its Authorized Users to access and
use the Platform, provided that Customer ensures each Authorized User complies
with the terms of this Agreement. Customer shall be responsible for all acts and
omissions of its Authorized Users as if they were the acts and omissions of
Customer.

2.3 Restrictions. Customer shall not, and shall not permit any third party to:

    (a) copy, modify, adapt, translate, or create derivative works based on the
    Platform or any part thereof;

    (b) reverse engineer, disassemble, decompile, or otherwise attempt to
    derive the source code, structure, or algorithms of the Platform;

    (c) sublicense, sell, resell, lease, rent, loan, distribute, or otherwise
    transfer rights to the Platform to any third party;

    (d) use the Platform for the benefit of any third party, including as part
    of a service bureau, time-sharing, or outsourcing arrangement;

    (e) remove, alter, or obscure any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on
    the Platform or Documentation;

    (f) use the Platform to store or transmit any Virus or any material that is
    unlawful, defamatory, or otherwise objectionable;

    (g) interfere with or disrupt the integrity or performance of the Platform
    or any data contained therein;

    (h) attempt to gain unauthorized access to the Platform, its related
    systems, or networks; or

    (i) use the Platform in violation of any applicable law, regulation, or
    industry standard.

2.4 Reservation of Rights. Provider retains all right, title, and interest in
and to the Platform, Documentation, and all related Intellectual Property
Rights. No rights are granted to Customer except as expressly set forth herein.


3. FEES AND PAYMENT

3.1 Fees. Customer shall pay Provider the fees specified in the applicable Order
Form ("Fees"). All Fees are quoted and payable in United States dollars.

3.2 Non-Refundable. All Fees paid under this Agreement are non-refundable,
regardless of the actual usage of the Services by Customer during any
subscription period, and regardless of whether Customer terminates this
Agreement prior to the expiration of the then-current Subscription Term.

3.3 Payment Terms. Unless otherwise specified in the applicable Order Form, all
Fees shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of Provider's
invoice. Customer shall make all payments by wire transfer or ACH to the account
designated by Provider.

3.4 Fee Increases. Provider may increase the Fees for any renewal Subscription
Term by providing Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice
before the commencement of such renewal term. If Customer does not agree to such
increase, Customer's sole remedy shall be to provide written notice of
non-renewal in accordance with Section 10.2.

3.5 Late Payments. Any amounts not paid when due shall accrue interest at the
rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted
by applicable law, whichever is less, from the date such payment was due until
the date paid.

3.6 Taxes. All Fees are exclusive of taxes. Customer shall be responsible for
all sales, use, value-added, withholding, and other taxes and government charges
arising from or relating to this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Provider's
net income.

3.7 Suspension for Non-Payment. If Customer fails to pay any undisputed Fees
when due and such failure continues for fifteen (15) days after written notice
thereof, Provider may suspend Customer's access to the Services until all
outstanding Fees are paid in full, without liability to Customer.


4. CUSTOMER DATA

4.1 Ownership. As between the Parties, Customer retains all right, title, and
interest in and to all Customer Data.

4.2 License to Customer Data. Customer hereby grants to Provider a non-exclusive,
worldwide, royalty-free license to use, copy, store, transmit, display, modify,
and create derivative works of Customer Data solely as necessary to provide the
Services and as otherwise permitted under this Agreement.

4.3 Data Security. Provider shall implement and maintain commercially reasonable
administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect Customer
Data from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction, in
accordance with industry standards.

4.4 Data Retention. Provider shall retain Customer Data during the Subscription
Term and for a period of ninety (90) days following the expiration or
termination of this Agreement ("Retention Period"). During the Retention Period,
Customer may request export of its Customer Data in a standard format. After the
Retention Period, Provider shall delete all Customer Data in its possession or
control within thirty (30) days, provided that Provider may retain anonymized or
aggregated data derived from Customer Data for its internal analytics purposes.

4.5 Data Breach Notification. In the event Provider becomes aware of any
unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data ("Data Breach"), Provider
shall notify Customer in writing within seventy-two (72) hours of discovering
such Data Breach and shall take commercially reasonable steps to investigate and
remediate the Data Breach.

4.6 Compliance. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection
laws and regulations in connection with its performance under this Agreement.


5. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

5.1 Provider IP. As between the Parties, Provider owns and shall retain all
right, title, and interest in and to the Platform, Documentation, Services,
and all related Intellectual Property Rights, including any improvements,
enhancements, modifications, or derivative works thereof, regardless of
whether such improvements are suggested or requested by Customer.

5.2 Customer IP Assignment. Customer hereby irrevocably assigns to Provider all
right, title, and interest, including all Intellectual Property Rights, in and
to all Work Product. Customer agrees to execute any documents and take any
actions reasonably requested by Provider to effectuate, perfect, or confirm
Provider's ownership of the Work Product. Customer hereby irrevocably appoints
Provider as Customer's attorney-in-fact, with full power of substitution, for
the purpose of executing such documents on Customer's behalf if Customer fails
to do so within ten (10) business days of Provider's request.

5.3 Usage Data. Provider shall own all right, title, and interest in and to all
Usage Data. Provider may use Usage Data for any lawful purpose, including to
improve the Platform and Services, develop new products and services, and
generate industry benchmarks and analytics, provided that such use does not
identify Customer or any individual Authorized User.

5.4 No Other Rights. Except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, neither
Party grants the other Party any rights, licenses, or interests in any
Intellectual Property Rights.


6. CONFIDENTIALITY

6.1 Obligations. Each Party (as "Receiving Party") agrees that during the term
of this Agreement and for a period of five (5) years thereafter, it shall:

    (a) hold all Confidential Information of the other Party (as "Disclosing
    Party") in strict confidence;

    (b) not disclose such Confidential Information to any third party without
    the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party, except to its employees,
    contractors, and advisors who have a need to know and who are bound by
    confidentiality obligations no less protective than those contained herein;

    (c) use such Confidential Information solely for the purposes contemplated
    by this Agreement; and

    (d) protect such Confidential Information using the same degree of care it
    uses to protect its own confidential information, but in no event less than
    a reasonable degree of care.

6.2 Exclusions. Confidential Information shall not include information that the
Receiving Party can demonstrate: (a) was publicly known at the time of
disclosure; (b) becomes publicly known through no fault of the Receiving Party;
(c) was in the Receiving Party's possession prior to disclosure; (d) was
received from a third party without breach of any obligation of
confidentiality; or (e) was independently developed by the Receiving Party
without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

6.3 Compelled Disclosure. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential
Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or court
order, provided that the Receiving Party gives the Disclosing Party prompt
written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permissible) and
cooperates with the Disclosing Party's efforts to obtain a protective order.


7. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

7.1 Mutual Representations. Each Party represents and warrants that: (a) it has
the legal power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) the
execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement does not conflict with
any other agreement to which it is a party; and (c) this Agreement constitutes
a valid and binding obligation enforceable against it in accordance with its
terms.

7.2 Provider Warranty. Provider warrants that the Platform will perform
materially in accordance with the Documentation during the Subscription Term.
Provider's sole obligation and Customer's sole remedy for a breach of this
warranty shall be for Provider to use commercially reasonable efforts to correct
the non-conformity, or, if Provider is unable to correct such non-conformity
within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice thereof, either Party may
terminate this Agreement.

7.3 Disclaimer. EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 7,
THE PLATFORM AND SERVICES ARE PROVIDED "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE." PROVIDER
MAKES NO OTHER WARRANTIES, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE,
INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A
PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, ACCURACY, RELIABILITY, OR
AVAILABILITY. PROVIDER DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE
UNINTERRUPTED, ERROR-FREE, OR SECURE, OR THAT ALL DEFECTS WILL BE CORRECTED.
CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT THE PLATFORM IS NOT DESIGNED OR INTENDED FOR USE IN
HIGH-RISK ACTIVITIES REQUIRING FAIL-SAFE PERFORMANCE.


8. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

8.1 Exclusion of Consequential Damages. IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE
LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL,
PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF
REVENUE, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL,
ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER BASED ON WARRANTY,
CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL
THEORY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

8.2 Cap on Liability. EXCEPT FOR OBLIGATIONS ARISING UNDER SECTION 9
(INDEMNIFICATION), IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING
OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE TOTAL FEES PAID OR
PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO PROVIDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTH PERIOD
IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.

8.3 Basis of the Bargain. THE LIMITATIONS SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 8 SHALL
APPLY NOTWITHSTANDING ANY FAILURE OF THE ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF ANY LIMITED REMEDY
AND SHALL CONSTITUTE A FUNDAMENTAL ELEMENT OF THE BASIS OF THE BARGAIN BETWEEN
THE PARTIES.


9. INDEMNIFICATION

9.1 Indemnification by Customer. Customer shall indemnify, defend, and hold
harmless Provider and its officers, directors, employees, agents, successors,
and assigns (collectively, "Provider Indemnitees") from and against any and all
claims, demands, actions, suits, proceedings, losses, damages, liabilities,
costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees and court costs)
("Losses") arising out of or in connection with:

    (a) Customer's use of the Platform or Services in violation of this
    Agreement;

    (b) Customer's breach of any representation, warranty, or obligation under
    this Agreement;

    (c) any claim that Customer Data infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise
    violates the Intellectual Property Rights or other rights of any third
    party;

    (d) Customer's violation of any applicable law, regulation, or industry
    standard in connection with its use of the Platform; or

    (e) any act or omission of Customer's Authorized Users in connection with
    the Platform or Services.

9.2 Indemnification Procedures. The indemnified party shall: (a) provide the
indemnifying party with prompt written notice of any claim; (b) grant the
indemnifying party sole control of the defense and settlement of such claim;
and (c) provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense. The
indemnified party may participate in the defense at its own expense with counsel
of its choice.


10. TERM AND TERMINATION

10.1 Initial Term. The initial Subscription Term shall be as specified in the
applicable Order Form, commencing on the Effective Date.

10.2 Automatic Renewal. Unless either Party provides written notice of
non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the
then-current Subscription Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for
successive renewal terms of twelve (12) months each (each, a "Renewal Term")
at the then-current Fees (subject to any increases under Section 3.4).

10.3 Termination by Provider. Provider may terminate this Agreement immediately
upon written notice to Customer if: (a) Customer fails to pay any undisputed
Fees within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of such failure;
(b) Customer breaches any material term of this Agreement and fails to cure
such breach within fifteen (15) days after receiving written notice thereof;
or (c) Customer becomes insolvent, files for bankruptcy, or has a receiver
appointed for a substantial part of its assets.

10.4 Termination by Customer. Customer may terminate this Agreement only at the
end of the then-current Subscription Term by providing written notice of
non-renewal in accordance with Section 10.2. Customer shall not have the right
to terminate this Agreement for convenience during any active Subscription Term.

10.5 Effect of Termination. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement:
(a) all rights and licenses granted to Customer hereunder shall immediately
terminate; (b) Customer shall immediately cease all use of the Platform and
Services; (c) Customer shall pay Provider all Fees accrued and owing through
the effective date of termination; and (d) each Party shall return or destroy
all Confidential Information of the other Party in its possession, subject to
Section 4.4.


11. NON-COMPETITION

11.1 Non-Compete Covenant. During the Subscription Term and for a period of
twenty-four (24) months following the expiration or termination of this
Agreement for any reason, Customer shall not, directly or indirectly, whether
alone or in conjunction with any other person or entity:

    (a) develop, design, produce, market, sell, offer for sale, license, or
    distribute any product or service that competes with or is substantially
    similar to the Platform or any component thereof;

    (b) solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any employee, contractor, or
    consultant of Provider who was involved in the development, support, or
    delivery of the Platform; or

    (c) induce or attempt to induce any customer or prospective customer of
    Provider to cease doing business with Provider or to reduce the amount of
    business such customer conducts with Provider.

11.2 Geographic Scope. The restrictions set forth in Section 11.1 shall apply
in any jurisdiction where Provider does business or has done business during the
twelve (12) months preceding the date of expiration or termination of this
Agreement, including any jurisdiction where Provider has customers, users,
marketing activities, or any other business presence.

11.3 Acknowledgment. Customer acknowledges that the restrictions contained in
this Section 11 are reasonable and necessary to protect Provider's legitimate
business interests, including its Confidential Information, customer
relationships, and goodwill, and that any violation of these restrictions would
cause irreparable harm to Provider for which monetary damages would be
inadequate.

11.4 Remedies. In the event of any breach or threatened breach of this
Section 11, Provider shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief and specific
performance, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity,
without the need to prove actual damages or post a bond.


12. FEEDBACK AND PERPETUAL LICENSE

12.1 Feedback License. Customer hereby grants to Provider an exclusive,
perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up,
sublicensable, and transferable license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt,
publish, translate, create derivative works from, distribute, perform, display,
import, sell, offer for sale, make, have made, and otherwise exploit any and
all Feedback for any purpose whatsoever, without restriction, obligation, or
compensation to Customer.

12.2 No Obligation. Provider shall have no obligation to use or incorporate any
Feedback. Customer acknowledges that Provider may have developed or received
from third parties ideas, suggestions, or materials similar to any Feedback,
and that Customer is not entitled to any compensation or credit for any
Feedback.

12.3 Waiver of Rights. To the extent permitted by applicable law, Customer
hereby waives and agrees not to assert any moral rights, rights of attribution,
rights of integrity, or any other rights of a similar nature in connection with
any Feedback.

12.4 Broad Interpretation. For purposes of this Section 12, "Feedback" shall be
interpreted broadly to include any ideas, suggestions, concepts, techniques,
methods, processes, or know-how communicated by Customer or any of its
Authorized Users to Provider in any form or medium, whether solicited or
unsolicited, including through use of the Platform, support interactions,
feature requests, surveys, or any other means of communication.


13. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

13.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in
accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its
conflict of laws principles.

13.2 Jurisdiction. Any legal action or proceeding arising out of or relating to
this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in the federal or state courts
located in Wilmington, Delaware, and each Party irrevocably submits to the
personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts.

13.3 Waiver of Jury Trial. EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY AND ALL
RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY LEGAL PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO
THIS AGREEMENT.


14. SURVIVAL

14.1 The following Sections shall survive the expiration or termination of this
Agreement: Section 1 (Definitions), Section 3 (Fees and Payment, to the extent
of any accrued obligations), Section 5 (Intellectual Property), Section 6
(Confidentiality), Section 8 (Limitation of Liability), Section 9
(Indemnification), Section 11 (Non-Competition), Section 12 (Feedback and
Perpetual License), Section 13 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution), this
Section 14 (Survival), and Section 15 (Miscellaneous).


15. MISCELLANEOUS

15.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with all Order Forms and
Exhibits attached hereto or incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire
agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and
supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings,
negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written.

15.2 Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended or modified except by a
written instrument signed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may update the SLA, Acceptable Use
Policy, and Privacy Policy from time to time by posting the updated version on
its website and providing Customer with thirty (30) days' prior written notice.

15.3 Waiver. No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right,
power, or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor
shall any single or partial exercise of any right, power, or remedy preclude
any other or further exercise thereof.

15.4 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid,
illegal, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full
force and effect. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any
invalid provision with a valid provision that most closely approximates the
intent and economic effect of the invalid provision.

15.5 Assignment. Customer may not assign or transfer this Agreement or any
rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of Provider,
which may be withheld in Provider's sole discretion. Provider may freely assign
this Agreement in connection with a merger, acquisition, corporate
reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets. Any
attempted assignment in violation of this Section shall be null and void.

15.6 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure to
perform its obligations under this Agreement (other than payment obligations)
to the extent caused by circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including
natural disasters, acts of government, war, terrorism, riots, epidemics,
pandemics, power failures, internet outages, and telecommunications failures.

15.7 Independent Contractors. The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing
in this Agreement shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture,
agency, franchise, or employment relationship between the Parties.

15.8 Notices. All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be
deemed given when: (a) delivered personally; (b) sent by confirmed email to the
email address specified in the applicable Order Form; or (c) sent by nationally
recognized overnight courier to the address set forth above, with a copy to
the legal department of the receiving Party.

15.9 Third-Party Beneficiaries. This Agreement is for the sole benefit of the
Parties and their permitted successors and assigns, and nothing herein is
intended to or shall confer upon any other person or entity any legal or
equitable right, benefit, or remedy of any nature whatsoever.

15.10 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts,
each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall
constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this
Agreement by electronic signature shall be deemed an original signature for all
purposes.

15.11 Headings. The headings in this Agreement are for convenience of reference
only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

15.12 Construction. This Agreement shall be construed without regard to any
presumption or other rule requiring construction against the drafting Party.
Each Party acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to review this Agreement
with legal counsel.

EXHIBIT A — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT

1. Availability. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain
Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and five-tenths percent (99.5%)
during each calendar month, measured on a 24x7 basis, excluding scheduled
maintenance windows.

2. Scheduled Maintenance. Provider shall perform scheduled maintenance during
the hours of 2:00 AM to 6:00 AM Eastern Time on Sundays. Provider shall provide
Customer with at least forty-eight (48) hours' prior notice of any scheduled
maintenance.

3. Support. Provider shall provide Customer with technical support via email
during regular business hours (9:00 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through
Friday, excluding federal holidays). Provider shall use commercially reasonable
efforts to respond to support requests within the following timeframes:

    Priority 1 (Critical): Platform is unavailable or a core function is
    completely non-functional — response within four (4) business hours.

    Priority 2 (High): A major function is significantly impaired but the
    Platform remains operational — response within eight (8) business hours.

    Priority 3 (Medium): A minor function is impaired or a workaround is
    available — response within two (2) business days.

    Priority 4 (Low): General questions, feature requests, or cosmetic
    issues — response within five (5) business days.

4. Service Credits. If Provider fails to meet the availability commitment in
any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit equal to:

    99.0% - 99.5% availability: 5% of monthly Fees
    95.0% - 99.0% availability: 10% of monthly Fees
    Below 95.0% availability: 20% of monthly Fees

Service credits shall be applied against future invoices and shall not exceed
twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Fees for the affected month. Service credits
are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for Provider's failure to meet the
availability commitment.
